rationale: Reading index 36 on nodes 1, 2 and 5 completes the picture and reveals a hole rather than a value. Those nodes report accepted 38 and decided 38, hold nothing at index 36, and hold the StopSign at index 37, while nodes 3 and 4 have 36 entries followed by the StopSign at index 36 and report accepted 37. An accepted index of 38 over a log with a gap at 36 and a StopSign at 37 is the signature of the known sync_log arithmetic that adds one for a StopSign on top of a prefix that already covers it, which inflates the accepted index by one without placing an entry. This update records the hole and the inflated accepted index, links them to that arithmetic, and restates the interpretation as a corrupt log plus an unsupported decided index rather than a simple divergent marker placement.

investigations.hypothesis: After a lossy reconfiguration, the sync path can inflate a group's accepted index by one without placing an entry, leaving a hole just before the StopSign. Nodes 1, 2 and 5 report accepted 38 with no entry at index 36 and the StopSign at 37, while nodes 3 and 4 hold 36 entries followed by the StopSign at 36 and report accepted 37. The inflated group's reported accepted index then lets the shorter group's leader decide 38 without a matching local entry, and the stalled follower's Decides are sequence-expected, so handle_decide clamps its decided index instead of reconnecting.

knowledge.assertion: Final observed state: nodes 1, 2 and 5 count 38 positions with index 36 absent and the StopSign at 37, while nodes 3 and 4 hold the StopSign at 36 and count 37. The accepted index of the first group is one higher than the number of positions it can actually read.

This is the source behavior that produces the observed shape: sync_log adds one for a StopSign on top of a prefix that already covers it, inflating accepted_idx without placing an entry, which is the hole seen at index 36.
Explains how node 4 reaches decided 38 with accepted 37 by counting the inflated group's reported accepted indices and setting its decided index without a matching local entry.

knowledge.statement: At the end of seeded run 13, nodes 1, 2 and 5 each report accepted 38 and decided 38, read index 36 as absent and read index 37 as a StopSign, while nodes 3 and 4 read index 36 as a StopSign, index 37 as absent and report accepted 37. Node 4 is decided 38. The group reporting accepted 38 therefore has no entry at index 36 yet counts 38 positions, and the StopSign appears one index later than on the other group.
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots; seed 0xbe5466cf34e90c6c, reconfigure at action 450 with 20 percent out-of-order loss, then 150 fair-delivery rounds; accepted and decided indices and entry kinds at indices 35, 36 and 37 are read once at the end for all five nodes.

interpretations.rationale: The executed receipts show a corrupt log layout and an unsupported decided index. Receipt 178cec2b468647b7852512ea21dee4b4 ran randomized_reconfig_diagnose_lag (exit 0, test passed); both declared comparisons are complete and violated, convergence because decided ended at 38,38,37,38,38 and the invariant because p4_gap is 1. The same event records nodes 1, 2 and 5 at accepted 38 and decided 38 with index 36 absent and a StopSign at index 37, and nodes 3 and 4 at accepted 37 with a StopSign at index 36 and index 37 absent. The group reporting accepted 38 therefore counts one more position than it can read: there is a hole at index 36 and the StopSign sits at 37, whereas the other group has 36 entries followed by the StopSign at 36. This is exactly the shape that sync_log's StopSign arithmetic produces when the sync prefix already covers the StopSign: it adds one to the accepted index without placing an entry, so the accepted index is inflated by one. Node 4, the final leader, merged a StopSign-bearing promise whose accepted index was 37 in round 3 and accepted a log ending with the StopSign at 36; it nevertheless reports decided 38 because handle_accepted takes the inflated group's reported accepted index once is_chosen counts a quorum, without comparing it to its own accepted index or requiring a matching local entry. Node 3, decided 37 with accepted 37, receives the Decides with sequence counters 2 and 3 as its next expected messages, so handle_decide clamps decided to 37; it sends no PrepareReq, is offered no AcceptStopSign because it already accepted one, and repeated Decides reuse a consumed sequence number, so it remains behind for the whole window. The zero divergence figure reported by earlier receipts is an artifact of the comparison helper, which keeps only Decided(Value) entries and compares the shorter prefix and therefore cannot see a hole, a StopSign at a different index or a prefix-length difference. The run therefore exhibits a corrupted log layout with an inflated accepted index on one group and a leader decided index that no local log supports, together with the follower stall that follows.
counterevidence: A follower that genuinely missed the AcceptStopSign can still recover: in the constructed clean-miss run the periodic Decide was sequence-ahead, the follower reconnected, and an AcceptSync repaired it.
A leadership change, or an external reconnected() call, leads to Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync, which gives the follower a fresh sequence and a log sync from the new leader.
The earlier zero divergence count is not counterevidence of agreement; it is an artifact of a comparison that ignores StopSign entries, holes and prefix lengths.
limitations: Indices and kinds are sampled once at the end, so the receipt shows the resulting hole and inflated accepted index but not the sync exchange that created them.
The exact log_sync content that inflated the accepted index was not recorded; the link to sync_log's StopSign arithmetic is inferred from the observed shape.
Node 3's inbound trace is capped at twelve messages after the lossy phase, and Promises to node 4 are recorded only when delivered and only up to forty entries.
Five nodes, MemoryStorage, unit batch, no snapshots and no next configuration started; flexible quorums, batching and snapshot-based sync are unexercised.
